title: Value Co-Creation and Service Relationships

header.html: Define value, value co-creation, cost, risk, output and outcome; explain how outcomes, costs, risks, utility, warranty, user experience, sustainability and feedback contribute to value co-creation; define organization, service provider, service consumer, digital product vendor, the three relationship types, the service journey, sponsor, customer, user, service quality, service level and SLA
the official ITIL Foundation (Version 5) syllabus, version 5.0 (February 2026), categories 1.4 and 1.5

toc.title: Relationship types and the service journey
Service quality, service level and SLA

html:
1Value and co-creation

Value is the perceived benefit, usefulness and importance of something. Value co-creation means value is created together by the provider and the consumer, through activities and interactions, not handed over by the provider alone.

Term Meaning
Output A tangible or intangible deliverable of an activity (a report, a working feature)
Outcome A result for a stakeholder enabled by one or more outputs (faster orders, fewer errors)
Cost What the consumer spends or gives up (money, time, effort), including the cost of creating the value
Risk A possible event that could cause harm or make achieving objectives harder
Exam tip

. Output = what you get. Outcome = what changes because of it. A new report is an output; better decisions are the outcome.

2What contributes to value

Contributor How it helps value co-creation
Outcomes The results the consumer wants
Costs Lower or justified costs raise perceived value
Risks Lower risk raises value
Utility The product does what is needed
Warranty It is available and dependable
User experience It is pleasant and easy to use
Sustainability It can be sustained over time without harm
Feedback Information from consumers shapes improvement and keeps the work aimed at value

3Who is who

Term Meaning
Organization A person or group with its own functions, responsibilities and goals
Service provider An organization that provides services to consumers
Service consumer An organization or person that consumes services
Digital product vendor An organization that supplies digital products (often as goods or access to resources)

A service provider runs the service for you. A digital product vendor supplies the product itself. A service consumer uses either, and may be the same organization as the provider in an internal setting.

Roles of the consumer

Role Responsibility
Sponsor Authorizes the budget for consumption
Customer Defines requirements and takes responsibility for the outcomes of consumption
User Uses the services

One person can hold more than one role.

Exam tip

. Sponsor pays. Customer decides what is needed. User uses.

4Relationship types and the service journey

Relationship Idea
Basic Transactional: the provider supplies, the consumer pays, little more
Cooperative Mutually beneficial; the parties share information and adjust to each other
Collaborative A partnership with shared goals and joint risk and reward

The service journey is the path a consumer and provider follow together, from the first contact to realized value. Beyond the syllabus The ITIL 4 journey steps were explore, engage, offer, agree, onboard, co-create and realize. [Verify live]

5Service quality, service level and SLA

Term Meaning
Service quality How well the service meets the consumer's needs and expectations
Service level A measurable statement of the level of service to be delivered
Service Level Agreement (SLA) A documented agreement between a provider and a customer naming the services and the expected service levels
Exam tip

. An SLA is an agreement; a service level is the target inside it.

6Exam Q&A

6.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1A new dashboard is delivered to the finance team, and decisions are now made two days faster. Which statement is right?

  • AThe dashboard is the outcome and the speed is the output
  • BBoth are outputs
  • CBoth are costs
  • DThe dashboard is the output and the faster decisions are the outcome
Show the answer

Answer: D. An output is the deliverable; the outcome is the result it enables.

S2Who defines the requirements for a service and takes responsibility for the outcomes of consumption?

  • AThe user
  • BThe sponsor
  • CThe customer
  • DThe vendor
Show the answer

Answer: C. The customer defines requirements and takes responsibility for outcomes.

S3Which statement about relationships is CORRECT? (1) A basic relationship is transactional. (2) A collaborative relationship is a partnership with shared goals. (3) A cooperative relationship has no sharing of information. (4) A basic relationship needs shared goals and joint risk.

  • A1 and 2
  • B2 and 3
  • C3 and 4
  • D1 and 4
Show the answer

Answer: A. Basic is transactional and collaborative is a partnership.

S4Identify the missing word(s). A [ ? ] authorizes the budget for service consumption.

  • AUser
  • BSponsor
  • CCustomer
  • DProvider
Show the answer

Answer: B. The sponsor authorizes the budget.

S5Customers give feedback and the provider changes the product. Which idea does this show?

  • AA transfer of goods
  • BA known error
  • CA basic relationship only
  • DValue co-creation, because feedback shapes what is created
Show the answer

Answer: D. Feedback is part of how value is co-created.

S6Which document names the services and the expected service levels between a provider and a customer?

  • AA product prototype
  • BA value stream map
  • CA practice guide
  • DA service level agreement
Show the answer

Answer: D. That is the SLA.

6.2 Recall questions

R1Define value co-creation.

Show the answer

Value created together by the provider and the consumer through activities and interactions.

R2Output or outcome: a result for a stakeholder?

Show the answer

Outcome.

R3What does the sponsor do?

Show the answer

Authorizes the budget for consumption.

R4Name the three relationship types.

Show the answer

Basic, cooperative and collaborative.

R5What is an SLA?

Show the answer

A documented agreement between a provider and a customer on services and expected service levels.

R6What are the seven contributors to value?

Show the answer

Outcomes, costs, risks, utility, warranty, user experience and sustainability (with feedback shaping them).

7Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Output / outcome deliverable / result for a stakeholder
Cost / risk what is spent or given up / possible harm
Roles sponsor pays, customer defines needs, user uses
Relationships basic (transaction), cooperative (mutual), collaborative (partnership)
SLA agreement; service level is the target
